feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level leadership and now consulting; this strengthens credibility and seniority.  
- Strong domain alignment: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently presented.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to make the CV tighter and easier to scan.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, newsletter performance, campaign results, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation choices, and serial comma usage. Minor wording polish: “A2/Learning” is awkward; use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly broad and repeats themes covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like stacking: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume communications.”
- Add clearer outcomes or scale from recent roles, e.g. “enterprise web modernization, analytics, and editorial systems supporting large, multi-publisher organizations.”
- Replace “AI-enabled user experiences” with a more specific phrase such as “AI-enabled search and content discovery experiences.”
- Consider this rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web modernization, digital governance, and content operations for high-volume communications. Builds and scales enterprise websites, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The service list closely repeats Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made slightly more specific, and framed around senior-level strengths rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with more distinctive strengths: “Editorial governance and publishing systems,” “Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure,” “Automation and platform integrations.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Editorial governance and publishing systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, drop one lower-priority item such as “Multi-channel communications operations,” which is implied elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and Recent Projects.
- Several items substantially duplicate Topline Skills, especially governance, analytics, automation, advocacy, and multimedia.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from role bullets.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and trim stacked nouns (e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat”).
- Where possible, add one concrete result, audience, or scale marker for each project.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work substantially overlap with current/previous NACo bullets; this section should emphasize project outcomes or unique features not stated elsewhere.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it or expanding it slightly.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it currently reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo leadership entry. Make it more clearly consultant-shaped, outcome-oriented, and focused on what is new since Jun. 2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + consulting value: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, content operations, and enterprise web optimization as an external consultant.”
- Replace generic verbs with deliverables: “Designed cross-channel workflows and analytics frameworks,” “Built Drupal microsite templates and modular content components,” “Led AI-enabled search discovery strategy.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, teams/stakeholders served, toolkit launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/adoption improvements.
- Tighten to 3–4 bullets, e.g. separate: strategy/governance, Drupal implementation, AI search initiative, analytics/workflow modernization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry unless tied to new consulting deliverables.
- CMS/front-end troubleshooting may feel too tactical unless framed as high-impact implementation for major public-facing properties.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale indicators. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the biggest wins and make them more results-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on infrastructure/process work: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast-quality video studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve performance visibility and decision-making.”
- If possible, add measurable outcomes for email/social/video/governance (growth %, engagement lift, production savings, faster publishing, reduced vendor costs).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language also overlaps with earlier NACo roles; emphasize studio buildout and organizational capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and systems built before promotion.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social, and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets and emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show impact: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is repeated in the Director role; vary by focusing here on day-to-day execution and workflow building.
- “weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the format rather than originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current strengths: enterprise governance, cross-channel leadership, and mission/public-sector strategy.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Cross-channel content operations leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered editorial planning
- Organizational messaging systems & standards
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel content operations leadership” to sound more specific and operational.
- Replace “Audience-focused” with “Audience-centered” or “User-centered” for cleaner phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale from recent roles rather than listing broad concepts alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Policy & advocacy communication”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your NACo work rather than repeat tool lists.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platforms-only to capability-led wording: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation.
- Drop lower-priority items unless they are job-targeted; “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and “Power Pages” are less supported by recent experience here.
- If space allows, sharpen one phrase for impact: replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and structured content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost line-for-line; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventories for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” and “workflow automation” also echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns well with the recent Director/Consultant roles, but it reads as a raw tool list. It would be stronger if framed around business value and kept distinct from the broader “Data analytics & reporting” competency.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder for impact: lead with outcomes, then tools. Example heading content: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive dashboards, SEO/performance analysis, GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider tightening to 6–7 items max; “Insights & Optimization” already implies analysis, so avoid overlisting adjacent terms.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to a measurable result from NACo (e.g., analytics infrastructure supporting 3.5M annual page views and strategic decision-making).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies; this item should stay more tool- and outcome-specific.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may partially duplicate broader digital strategy language unless positioned as a distinct optimization capability.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production environment and delivery scope rather than listing broad video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Hybrid/virtual event production • Studio operations and run-of-show execution”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrasing like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match director-level experience.
- Add one scope cue if space allows: “for advocacy programming, member events, and recurring multimedia content.”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools (“PTZ camera systems”) with broad functions unless all bullets follow the same format.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies; consider trimming one or differentiating this section as execution-focused.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already implied by the NACo studio-building bullet, so avoid repeating that story elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize platform administration/publishing systems or removed if space is tight.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web CMS & Publishing Platforms
- Revise content to: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If you want stronger impact, prioritize the most credible/recent platform first and consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it was used professionally at meaningful scale.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the separate coding/technical section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles; avoid repeating too many generic platform names without context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current, implementation-focused, and specific to tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation & Web Operations
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in current work.
- If space allows, add light context for impact: “front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment automation” rather than only listing tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills overlaps with GitHub Actions here; keep this item tool-specific and let Topline Skills stay broader.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems-building relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Workflow automation & collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Team operations: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Put the highest-value, most differentiating tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier.
- Standardize naming for professionalism: “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”
- If accurate, add scope in another section rather than here, e.g., “built cross-team workflows” or “automated reporting/intake processes,” since outcomes matter more than listing every platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar category tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and undersells your email/engagement leadership. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, frame these as platforms used to run large-scale communications, not just tools you know.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: Enterprise email campaign management • newsletter operations • audience segmentation • journey automation
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel claims in Core Competencies and Work Experience; avoid adding generic phrases like “digital engagement” here
- Don’t repeat newsletter scale or audience size in this skills item; those metrics belong in the NACo experience bullets

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it to emphasize technical tools here and leave strategy/outcomes to recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis**; “SEO” is too broad for a technical tools line.
- Remove **Dashboarding** unless you rename it to **dashboard development**; current phrasing is vague and redundant with Looker Studio/Power BI.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently used stack: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills entry; consider trimming one or making this one tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating broad terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with clearer outcomes if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social media, and multimedia production.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete contributions: website refresh, livestream/event production, weekly video content, and junior staff support.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of livestreams/events produced, frequency/audience of weekly videos, size/scope of website refresh, or turnaround/process improvements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting content production and workflows across web, email, social, and video. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on production rather than channel expansion.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify what changed or cut it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital content roles. Emphasize the innovation/research scope and make the podcast launch the clearest outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities…”
- Tighten the multimedia phrasing; avoid “contributed to” if possible. Use stronger verbs like “produced,” “developed,” or “supported.”
- Make the podcast the anchor achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add volume or reach: number of episodes, internal stakeholders supported, or types of deliverables produced.

Possible rewrite
- Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities, while producing digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia here if those accomplishments are better established in 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills, so keep this entry software/tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast recording/editing**
